question: Primary PCI is preferred over thrombolysis in STEMI if it can be performed within 120 minutes of first medical contact, even at a non-PCI-capable centre requiring transfer.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is actually true. The 120-minute FMC-to-device time is the threshold: if achievable (including transfer), primary PCI is preferred. If transfer would cause delay beyond 120 min, immediate fibrinolysis + transfer for coronary angiography within 3–24 h is recommended.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Guidelines recommend primary PCI if total first-medical-contact-to-device time is ≤120 minutes. If transfer will cause this window to exceed 120 minutes, immediate fibrinolysis should be performed instead (pharmacoinvasive strategy).
